services.desc: The Nave Museum is collaborating with The Vine School to bring their students fun and engaging art activities! These classes will take place right after school is over. Students will get to work with a variety of mediums such as clay, paint, crafts, snack-making, and so much more! This is a program for Vine School students only! Children from any of The Vine School's programs are welcome to attend. Classes are held every Monday or Thursday (depending on age group) during the semester, 2:15 - 3 pm, in the Vine School main campus. $50 per child to register. services.name: Past Exhibits
services.desc: For many, the most striking permanent exhibit at The Nave Museum is the building itself. A popular stop for photographers and lovers of architecture, the building was designed as a majestic Greek revival temple by San Antonio architect, Atlee Ayers. It opened to the public in 1932. Scattered around the building grounds are two monument sculptures by Texas artist, Mac Whitney. Mr. Whitney’s work has been exhibited in shows throughout the United States and Europe and, in addition to The Nave, he has permanent collections at the Dallas Museum of Art, The Fort Worth Museum of Art, The Witte Memorial Art Museum, and the University of North Texas Museum.
